title: The consultant who left
scenario:
You manage AI tools at a 40-person consulting firm. Most staff use a ChatGPT Enterprise workspace. The legal team uses Claude on a Team plan. Your company directory (the identity provider) adds and removes people in ChatGPT. Four access tickets wait in your queue.

Use the exhibit. The firm, people and tickets are made up for this case. Product facts are from the vendors' help pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
ACCESS TICKETS (made up)

  #1 ChatGPT  Priya moved her "Proposal checker" GPT
     to a plugin yesterday. Her team says they can't
     find it, though they all used the old GPT.

  #2 ChatGPT  Marco left last week. His manager asks:
     "Who owns Marco's 'Bid tracker' project now?
     Do I get his private chats with it?"

  #3 ChatGPT  IT removed Marco in Workspace settings >
     Members. The directory still lists him in the
     'Consultants' group that grants ChatGPT access.

  #4 Claude   The 'Client fees' project was shared with
     12 invited people. The Claude Owner turned
     off project sharing for the whole org. All 12
     still see it.

questions.prompt: Ticket 1: why can't Priya's team find the plugin?

options.text: A new plugin starts private, so Priya must share it again
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI: your new plugin starts private. Share it with the people who need it, even if they used the old GPT.

options.text: The team keeps access but must wait one day for it to sync
options.explanation: No page describes a one-day wait. The plugin starts private until it is shared.

options.text: Plugins can't be shared; each person must rebuild their own
options.explanation: The ChatGPT docs say people with Share plugins access can share a plugin with people or groups.

options.text: Old GPT access moves over, so the team is using a bad link
options.explanation: The ChatGPT docs say the plugin starts private. Access to the old GPT does not carry over.

questions.prompt: Ticket 2: what do you tell Marco's manager?

options.text: The project is deleted, along with all of Marco's chats
options.explanation: The ChatGPT docs say removing workspace access isn't the same as deleting content. The project is reassigned.

options.text: A workspace owner now owns it; Marco's private chats stay private
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI reassigns a leaver's projects to a workspace owner, but does not transfer their private conversations or files.

options.text: The manager owns it now and can read all of Marco's chats
options.explanation: Ownership goes to a workspace owner, and private conversations are not transferred.

options.text: Nobody owns it until Marco signs in and hands it over himself
options.explanation: The ChatGPT docs say the workspace reassigns ownership automatically when a member leaves.

questions.prompt: Ticket 3: what is the risk, and the fix?

options.text: None; a removal in Workspace settings is always final
options.explanation: The ChatGPT docs warn that a later directory sync can restore a member removed only from the workspace.

options.text: His chats will be deleted at the next sync; export them now
options.explanation: The pages warn about access coming back, not chats being deleted.

options.text: A sync can add him back; remove him from the directory group
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI: if you remove the member only from the workspace, a later sync can restore access. Remove him in the identity provider.

options.text: Delete the whole Consultants group so the sync stops working
options.explanation: That would cut off every other consultant too. Remove only Marco from the group in the identity provider.

questions.prompt: Ticket 4: why do all 12 people still see the project?

options.text: The switch takes a week, and then all 12 will lose access
options.explanation: No page describes a delay like that. Existing access stays until someone removes it.

options.text: Turning sharing off only hides the project from search results
options.explanation: The Claude Help Center says projects already shared stay shared, and people with access keep it.

options.text: Sharing settings only apply to Enterprise plans, not to Team
options.explanation: The Claude Help Center describes project sharing on both Team and Enterprise plans.

options.text: Existing shares stay; remove the people in the project itself
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: projects that are already shared stay shared, and users with access keep it. Remove them in the project itself.
